players.product: Advantage2 annealing quantum computers and dual-rail superconducting gate-model systems (Quantum Circuits)

quarterly_data.signal: D-Wave (10-K): launched its sixth-generation annealing quantum computing system Advantage2 in May 2025 (20-way connectivity); its QPUs can be deployed on-premises or accessed through the Leap quantum cloud service (99.9% availability); on January 20, 2026 it completed the acquisition of Quantum Circuits, Inc., adding dual-rail superconducting gate-model qubits to its gate-model program.

Supplier SkyWater Technology: D-Wave uses SkyWater Technology Foundry's services to manufacture wafers and for other services related to SkyWater's semiconductor line, under a Semiconductor Line Operation Agreement that renews automatically for one-year periods unless either party gives six months' notice (either party may also terminate for convenience on one year's notice).

D-Wave (10-K): other named customers and deployments - its customer list also includes Interpublic Group and BBVA; Florida Atlantic University signed an agreement (January 2026) to purchase and install an Advantage2 system at its Boca Raton campus, deployment expected later in 2026; in October 2025 it agreed with Swiss Quantum Technology SA to deploy an Advantage2 system in Europe with an option for SQT to purchase it; the Julich Supercomputing Centre owns a D-Wave Advantage system, upgraded to Advantage2 during 2025; PWC, Carahsoft and Staque are also named among the firms D-Wave sells with or through.

connects_to.relationship: D-Wave hybrid-quantum application optimizing a BASF liquid-filling facility; BASF is a named D-Wave customer

contracts.signal: D-Wave (10-K): BASF, a named customer, built a hybrid-quantum application to optimize manufacturing workflows in a BASF liquid-filling facility; it reduced lateness by 14%, setup times by 9% and tank unloading durations by up to 18% versus the existing optimization solution, and cut production scheduling time from 10 hours to seconds.

connects_to.relationship: D-Wave annealing quantum computing for mobile-network paging optimization (pilot; production deployment planned)

contracts.signal: D-Wave (10-K): NTT DOCOMO, Japan's largest mobile phone operator and a named customer, used D-Wave's annealing quantum computing to cut paging signals at base stations during peak calling times by 15 percent in pilot tests (Tokai, Chugoku and Kyushu regions), allowing approximately 1.2 times more terminals to connect; the hybrid solver finished in 40 seconds a task a general-purpose solver took 27 hours, and DOCOMO plans to deploy the solution in production across its Japanese branch offices.

connects_to.relationship: D-Wave hybrid quantum application for Ford Transit production sequencing

contracts.signal: D-Wave (10-K): Turkey-based Ford Otosan (a Ford Motor Company / Koc Holding joint venture and a named customer) and D-Wave built a hybrid quantum application to optimize production sequencing of the Ford Transit van line that scheduled 1,000 vehicles per run in under 5 minutes, compared to 30 minutes with the existing process.

connects_to.relationship: D-Wave Leap hybrid solvers in production for grocery delivery and in-store scheduling

contracts.signal: D-Wave (10-K): Pattison Food Group, a named customer, uses hybrid solvers in the Leap service (Advantage QPU) and has moved several quantum hybrid applications into production - an e-commerce driver delivery scheduling application serving over 100 stores that cut an 80-hour weekly task to 15 hours, and an in-store resource scheduling application across its stores in Canada.

connects_to.relationship: D-Wave Advantage2 quantum computer hosted at Davidson Technologies in Huntsville, Alabama; named D-Wave customer

contracts.signal: D-Wave (10-K): since November 2025 Davidson Technologies, a named customer, hosts the second U.S.-based D-Wave Advantage2 quantum computer at its global headquarters in Huntsville, Alabama, which will eventually run sensitive applications; D-Wave also sells with or through Davidson Technologies (who hosts a system node).
